name: rosetta-operator-precedence
code:
use default

// Precedence and associativity are inferred from how an operator
// is spelled, generally from its first character, and are
// resolved in the parser, before operator definitions are
// handled. Operators that start with `+` have 'addition'
// precedence wherever and however they are defined; similarly,
// operators that start with `<` have 'relational' precedence.
// Precedence can be overridden locally with the `@precedence`
// pragma, but that overrides it for every operator with that
// spelling, not for one specific overload.

row(level: string, ops: string, assoc: string) -> string =>
    "  {level,-16}{ops,-30}{assoc}"

levels() -> Pipe[string] is
    yield row("primary", "f(x)  a[i]  (e)  T(x)", "left")
    yield row("postfix", ".  ?.  ?  !  |>", "left")
    yield row("prefix", "!  -  any spelling", "right")
    yield row("user-8", "", "left")
    yield row("multiplication", "*  /  %", "left")
    yield row("user-7", "", "left")
    yield row("addition", "+  -", "left")
    yield row("user-6", "", "left")
    yield row("bitwise", "&  |  ^", "left")
    yield row("user-5", "an unrecognised spelling", "left")
    yield row("shift", "<<  >>  >>>", "left")
    yield row("user-4", "", "left")
    yield row("range", "..  ::  ..<  ::<", "left")
    yield row("user-3", "", "left")
    yield row(
        "relational", "==  !=  =~  !~  <  <=  >  >=", "left")
    yield row("user-2", "", "left")
    yield row("boolean", "/\\  \\/", "left")
    yield row("user-1", "??", "right")
si

// This class leverages the compiler's expression parsing and
// operator precedence to show the actual precedence applied: its
// `to_string()` shows the parentheses placed according to the
// order `***` and `<+>` actually bind in.
class E is
    text: string

    init(text: string) is self.text = text; si

    to_string() -> string => text

    // A static operator member takes both operands as
    // arguments.
    ***(a: E, b: E) -> E static => joined("***", a, b)

    // An instance operator member takes the left operand as
    // receiver.
    <+>(other: E) -> E => joined("<+>", self, other)
si

joined(op: string, a: E, b: E) -> E => E("({a} {op} {b})")

// A global operator.
+++(a: E, b: E) -> E => joined("+++", a, b)

// A leading `?` groups rightwards.
?+(a: E, b: E) -> E => joined("?+", a, b)

<*>(a: E, b: E) -> E => joined("<*>", a, b)

grouping(a: E, b: E, c: E) -> Pipe[string] is
    yield "  a +++ b *** c   {a +++ b *** c}"
    yield "  a <+> b +++ c   {a <+> b +++ c}"
    yield "  a +++ b +++ c   {a +++ b +++ c}"
    yield "  a ?+ b ?+ c     {a ?+ b ?+ c}"
    yield "  a <*> b *** c   {a <*> b *** c}"
si

// `@precedence` overrides the precedence of all implementations
// of one operator spelling within its scope.
@precedence("<*>", "user-8")
lifted(a: E, b: E, c: E) -> string =>
    "  a <*> b *** c   {a <*> b *** c}"

class BOX is
    value: int public

    init(value: int) is self.value = value; si
si

// Arguments are passed by value: a callee that assigns to its
// parameter changes only its own copy. A `ref` argument passes the
// variable itself. A class value is a reference, so a callee can
// still change the fields of the object it refers to.
assign(n: int mut) is n = 99; si
assign_through(n: int ref) is n! = 99; si
set_field(b: BOX) is b.value = 99; si

entry() is
    write_line("precedence, highest first")
    write_line("")

    levels() |> each(l => write_line(l))

    write_line("")
    write_line("the grouping the parser chose")
    write_line("")

    let a = E("a")
    let b = E("b")
    let c = E("c")

    grouping(a, b, c) |> each(l => write_line(l))

    write_line("")
    write_line("the same expression, under @precedence")
    write_line("")
    write_line(lifted(a, b, c))

    write_line("")
    write_line("arguments are passed by value")
    write_line("")

    let n mut = 1
    let m mut = 1
    let box = BOX(1)

    assign(n)
    assign_through(m ref)
    set_field(box)

    write_line("  callee assigned to an int          {n}")
    write_line("  callee assigned through an int ref {m}")
    write_line("  callee set a field of a class      {box.value}")
si
